thread:
samantha.support: P1 escalation — customer reports missing audit events in their Splunk index after we rolled out export filtering yesterday. They see a gap from 2026-03-05T10:12:00Z to 10:20:00Z. Attached: sample event IDs and request IDs. Can eng/security triage? cc @josh.security @priya.support

priya.support: Thanks. Can you paste the sample event IDs + which export config they were using? Was this the s3-forwarder -> splunk connector path or the SIEM direct export?

samantha.support: Sample event IDs: evt_8f3a2, evt_8f3a9, evt_8f4b0. Export config: splunk-connector v2.3.1, export_filter: 'severity>=INFO and not user:internal'. Customer says some admin events (high-severity) were dropped.

josh.security: Looking. First question: did we rotate the KMS key for audit-bucket around that time? If so the forwarder may have skipped decrypts during the key transition. @kevin.infra?

kevin.infra: We rotated the key at 10:15Z. Rotation was configured for dual-key decrypts but forwarder logs show an error at 10:15:12 for batch b-312. Pasting log snippet: 
```json
{"ts":"2026-03-05T10:15:12Z","level":"error","component":"audit-forwarder","err":"decrypt: ciphertext header missing kms-tag","batch":"b-312"}
```

priya.support: That aligns with the reported gap. Why would it affect only some events (admin ones)? Could be related to how the transformer runs.

josh.security: Two hypotheses: 1) During decryption error the forwarder emits a reduced placeholder event that strips user fields; downstream Splunk props/filters might drop events without user/admin fields. 2) Some objects retried successfully, others exceeded retry limits and were marked dropped. Need to check forwarder retry behavior and splunk-side filtering.

audit-forwarder-bot: delivery_status: batch b-312 -> errored (decrypt), retry scheduled at 2026-03-05T10:16:42Z, retry_count=1; final_status: dropped after 3 retries due to missing header. Logs: /ops/forwarder/logs/b-312

kevin.infra: Pulling forwarder config now. Relevant snippet: 
```ini
[forwarder]
retries = 3
drop_on_error = false
transformer = remove_internal_fields_v1
```
Note: transformer runs before delivery. If decryption fails we currently attach header "kms_missing:true" and emit a placeholder event. That placeholder loses some fields.

samantha.support: Customer wants the exact list of dropped event IDs and a mitigation plan. Can we furnish those quickly and offer a workaround?

josh.security: Action plan: 1) Confirm dropped event IDs from the export manifest in S3 (I will run the query). 2) Kick a re-decrypt/re-ingest job for affected objects from S3 backup. 3) Recommend temporary Splunk index rule to accept events with kms_missing:true. 4) Fix forwarder to preserve original headers on decrypt failure and not strip user/admin fields. I'll open INF ticket.

priya.support: Paste the query/command you used for step 1 so I can include it in the customer update. They'll want CSV of IDs.

josh.security: Query I ran against exports metadata DB: 
```sql
SELECT object_key, event_id FROM audit_exports WHERE ts BETWEEN '2026-03-05T10:10:00Z' AND '2026-03-05T10:25:00Z' AND status='dropped' AND reason LIKE '%kms%';
```
Result: evt_8f3a2, evt_8f3a9, evt_8f4b0, evt_8f4c1

kevin.infra: Kicked re-decrypt job for batch b-312 -> job id: rejob-2026-03-05-744. ETA ~45m. Will post status updates.

samantha.support: I'll update customer with the four event IDs and the ETA. Also offering a temporary Splunk rule snippet they can apply.

josh.security: Opened ticket INF-2026-437 for the long-term fix (preserve headers, adjust retry semantics). Also adding an item to docs: note to customers to not filter on missing kms headers.

priya.support: Marking P1 until reingest completes and customer confirms events are present in SIEM. :thumbsup:

samantha.support: Thanks all — I'll close the loop once customer confirms. Keeping thread open for updates.
